records.summary: The Magisk module and companion app behind the XDA thread. It contains the only working third-party client for the Stylo 2 haptics service found so far.
details: app/src/main/java/com/oplus/ipemanager/sdk/ holds the reconstructed service interface: ISdkAidlInterface, ISDKAidlCallback, Vibration and IpeFeature. The files are marked as cleaned reconstructions.
OplusPencilSdkClient.kt defines StylusVibrationClient: permission check, bindService, interface-descriptor check, and a StateFlow<Connection> for the UI.
The README says the vibration presets were taken from analysis of the stock OnePlus Notes app.
Build: Kotlin, minSdk 30, targetSdk 36, compileSdk 36, AGP 8.13.0, Kotlin 2.0.21.
Known defect: unbind() calls stopVibration() after unbindService(), so the stop command can go to a binder that is already released. Stop first, then unbind.
Known defect: getSupportFeatureList() is declared but has no transaction code and always throws.
The non-root interoperability track sits alongside this app: see repo-stylo2-interop-track. It does not use the Magisk module or the priv-app install.
records.basis: Read in full from the repository on 2 Nov 2026. Extended on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: Non-root interoperability track: stylo2 Rust workspace and Android test apps
records.summary: The Rust library and the three Android modules that the route docs are written around. They are host-tested only; nothing has run on a device.
details: stylo2/ is a Rust workspace with five crates: stylo2-core (API, states, profiles, errors, backend trait, command policy), stylo2-oplus (binder adapter and the profile-to-integer mapping), stylo2-ble (direct-BLE scaffold, inert until a verified profile is supplied, plus a ranker for discovered characteristics), stylo2-android (backend choice and tablet-vibrator fallback), stylo2-ffi (C ABI and optional JNI entry points).

android/ holds stylo2-bridge (Kotlin layer), stylo2-poc (Route A PoC) and stylus-ble-inspector (BLE inspector). They are modules of one Gradle build at the repository root, next to the upstream app in app/.

Android build status, as the docs now state it: the ledger, the root README and the PoC and inspector READMEs say the modules compile (assembleDebug, from the repository root) and the inspector's JVM unit tests pass, from a Gradle run on 2 Nov 2026. All say not device-tested. This record did not re-run Gradle. An earlier version of the ledger said the modules were not built.
Host check on 2 Nov 2026: cargo test --workspace ran 26 tests and all passed (core 15, ble 4, ffi 3, android 2, oplus 2).
Same day: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets with warnings denied finished clean. The jni feature check could not run offline here, so that claim is unchecked.
Doc inconsistency: stylo2/README.md and docs D, E and F say 22 tests. PICKUP.md and G say 26. The code and the run say 26.

Where device results go in code: stylo2_ble::Stylo2GattProfile (service UUID, control characteristic UUID, byte encoder; deliberately no default value), stylo2_ble::recon::candidate_control_characteristics (ranks discovered characteristics), the BinderTransport and GattTransport traits, stylo2_oplus::wire::reported_code, and Availability.ble_protocol_verified in stylo2-android.

wire::reported_code returns Pencil 0, Eraser 1, Ballpoint 2, Pen 3. Its doc comment says these are inferred from declaration order. A separate constant gives 4 for FUNCTION_VIBRATION and calls it a feedback mode, which is unconfirmed (gap-oneplus-feature-semantics).
ConnectionState has five states today: Disconnected, Connecting, Connected, PermissionDenied, ServiceUnavailable.
stylo2_android::preferred_backend picks the authorised binder first, then verified direct BLE, then the tablet vibrator, which is labelled as not the pen.

Boundaries stated in the docs: no root, no priv-app install, no firmware change. The PoC calls the system service only. The inspector is an ordinary BLE client. Licence: stylo2/README.md says the workspace is dual-licensed Apache-2.0 or MIT, and the root README says the repository has no licence of its own yet. The inspector bundles two MIT-licensed BlueShark files (see its NOTICE).
Read-only tablet tooling lives in research/tools/pad3_readout.py (plan-pad3-readout).
records.basis: stylo2/ and android/ read, and cargo test and cargo clippy run on the host, on 2 Nov 2026. Android modules not rebuilt here. Nothing run on a device.

records.summary: Tools for seeing what an already-paired pen and the tablet exchange over Bluetooth.
details: Because the Stylo 2 is already connected, Android's own HCI snoop log is the first choice. An external sniffer is a fallback if the log is not detailed enough.

BlueShark (MIT, nphil) with Shizuku captures the HCI snoop on a stock tablet without root, with named markers and a decode down to ATT (per stylo2/docs/G-local-continuation.md). Shizuku is started over ADB and is not root. Not tried here. Both are extra apps, so ask the owner first.
The BLE inspector in android/stylus-ble-inspector reuses two BlueShark files (see its NOTICE) but is not a sniffer. A second GATT client cannot see Notes' traffic.
J: an external sniffer only adds value if the HCI snoop misses packets, and over-the-air capture of an encrypted link shows ciphertext unless pairing was captured.

records.title: fix-odm-oplus-pad2pro (Stylus Fixes for OnePlus, v1.2)
records.summary: The Magisk module from the XDA regional-ROM thread. It copies pen firmware the ROM already has into a directory named after the tablet's own project number, then overlays that onto /odm/firmware.
details: Author jjhitel (Jeong Seongpil). GPL-3.0. v1.0 to v1.2, 4 to 19 Aug 2025. A reference copy of the scripts is in research/reference/fix-odm-oplus-pad2pro/.
Install (customize.sh): reads ro.boot.prjname. Aborts unless it is five digits and ro.product.system.manufacturer is oplus.
Lists the other five-digit directories in /odm/firmware/wireless_pen/, sorted. With one, it uses it. With several, it is meant to take the next untried one on each re-flash, tracked by marker files.
Copies every *.bin from the chosen directory into the module's odm/firmware/wireless_pen/<prjname>/, with SELinux context vendor_configs_file.

Every boot (post-fs-data.sh): mounts an overlay on /odm/firmware with its upper layer in /dev/anyfs (RAM), so the new directory appears alongside the stock ones. It does this mount itself instead of relying on the root manager.
Ships no firmware. It only reuses files already on the tablet.

History: v1.0 supported only the OnePlus Pad 2 Pro (prjname 24926 or 24976). It copied 24976's file into 24926 and forced ro.boot.prjname=24976. v1.1 added the overlay mount (credit AestasBritannia). v1.2 made it generic and stopped forcing the property.

Caveats found in the code: re-flash marker files probably don't survive, because Magisk empties the module folder on each install, so it may always pick the lowest-numbered directory. With no other directory it still reports success. On a tablet that already has its own directory, it replaces that firmware with another variant's.
It doesn't check firmware compatibility, so a successful install doesn't prove the chosen file is right.
Full write-up: research/docs/pen-attach-handshake.md
records.basis: Uploaded v1.2 zip (SHA-256 9371189d…6484331) compared with the GitHub repo at commit 0131a9d; scripts identical. Read 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: README.md: project basis and scope
records.summary: The repository's own statement of the basis, the in-scope routes and the out-of-scope items for the haptics research.
details: Path: README.md at the repository root.

Basis as stated: on a Pad 3 everything the Stylo 2 does works in every app except haptics, which work only in OnePlus Notes and a few approved apps. Pen input is an uplink through Android's stylus stack. Haptics are a control command to the pen, routed through com.oplus.ipemanager and protected by com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT.

It then says the motor, the command path and the Bluetooth link work and that what a third-party app lacks is authorisation, and marks this as resting on the owner's report until the first on-device session confirms it. This database holds it as unverified (c-trust-boundaries).

Routes in scope: A, unprivileged binder (android/stylo2-poc); B, direct Bluetooth LE (android/stylus-ble-inspector and J); C, official authorisation (B-feasibility); and the tablet-vibrator fallback, labelled as not the pen.

Out of scope: bypassing safe.IOT, the service's caller checks or OnePlus's app authentication; root, Magisk, priv-app or firmware changes as the delivery method; re-implementing pen input; sending the pen bytes nobody has observed.

Its status section says the Rust workspace builds with 26 passing tests, the Android modules compile, and the read-out tool runs against a simulated device. All are host claims (repo-stylo2-interop-track).
It maps the database status verified to include a read-out from a real device.
Status here describes the document as a source: written without a device, so its device claims are unchecked. Each claim is tracked in the records listed under related.
Licence, as stated: not settled. The Cargo manifests declare Apache-2.0 OR MIT, but there are no LICENSE files and the rest of the repository declares none.

records.title: CLAUDE.md: standing rules for work on the tablet and the data
records.summary: The rules every session follows: no cracking, a read-only tablet, ask before changes, pen writes only from captured bytes, honest status labels.
details: Path: CLAUDE.md at the repository root. Read in full on 2 Nov 2026.

No cracking: no bypassing signature, permission or app-authentication checks, and no extracting or reusing vendor signing keys, certificates or tokens. A route that needs any of that is recorded as a finding and stopped. No patching OnePlus apps or firmware. One owner-approved decompiling exception (2 Nov 2026): JADX on the tablet's own copy of com.oplus.ipemanager, interface classes only, recording only names, codes and signatures via research/tools/aidl_check.py. Reading an APK's public signer fingerprint still needs the owner's go-ahead.
The tablet is read-only. Allowed reads: getprop, ls, cat, dumpsys, pm path and pm list, logcat -d, dmesg, modinfo, sha256sum, find, adb pull. research/tools/pad3_readout.py enforces this.
Ask the owner first before installing or uninstalling an app (including this repository's own apps), changing a setting (including the HCI snoop log), starting Shizuku, or writing to the pen.
Root is never needed for what the project ships. If the tablet is rooted, su may be used for reads only.
Pen writes: only bytes captured from OnePlus Notes on this device. No fuzzing.
Never report an unauthorised or failed call as success. Works means the pen physically vibrated. Pen input and Notes must keep working; if probing disrupts them, stop and tell the owner.

Data: pulled files go in research/local/ and are never committed; redact Bluetooth addresses, serial numbers, IMEIs and account names; set status honestly (verified only for what was read or observed on the device, with build and date in basis); set updated on every changed record.
Code: do not change AIDL transaction codes, interface descriptors or profile integers without device evidence. app/ is upstream code and is left unchanged unless the owner asks.

Effect on this database: the ledger's JADX experiment for Q10 is allowed in the narrowed form of PICKUP.md Step 2b (gap-aidl-matches-firmware), and the B0 comparison of signing certificates needs the owner's decision (c-trust-boundaries).
records.basis: CLAUDE.md read in full from the repository on 2 Nov 2026. It is a rules file; it makes no claims about the device.

records.title: stylo2/docs/B-feasibility.md: four routes compared
records.summary: Assessment of the four routes to the pen's motor under a stock, non-rooted, own-certificate constraint.

records.title: stylo2/docs/C-protocol.md: reported binder surface and BLE unknowns
records.summary: The reported OnePlus binder surface (binding facts, transaction table, profiles, callbacks) and the unknown direct-BLE surface, with a recon procedure.
details: Path: stylo2/docs/C-protocol.md.

Part 1 marks the package, action and service component verified in the repository, and the gating permission verified in the repository with its level reported (at least privileged). The descriptor, the 12 transaction codes, the profile integers and the callbacks are marked reported.

Part 1.5 lists read-only checks to upgrade reported items: the permission level through dumpsys package and the framework permission XML; the service and descriptor through dumpsys activity services; the profile integers through setVibrationType 0 to 4 on an authorised binding.

Part 2: no UUIDs, characteristics or encodings are known and none are invented. Direct BLE needs five things to hold: the pen is observable to an ordinary app, a second client can discover its GATT while it is bonded to the system, a writable characteristic drives the motor, the payload encoding is known, and a second connection does not disrupt the system link.
Part 3: the reported interface has no intensity, duration, frequency, waveform or custom-pattern parameter, so the library leaves those capabilities off.
It calls FUNCTION_VIBRATION (4) a feedback mode rather than a profile. This database treats that as unconfirmed (gap-oneplus-feature-semantics).

records.title: stylo2/docs/H-trust-boundaries.md: boundaries and isolating experiment
records.summary: Architecture sketch of the binder and direct-BLE paths, the boundary table B0 to B4 with enforcement points, and the four-step isolating experiment.
details: Path: stylo2/docs/H-trust-boundaries.md.
Two candidate paths to the motor: the binder path (how Notes works) crosses B1 and B2, then B3 and B4; the direct-BLE path tries to reach B3 and B4 without B1 and B2.

Boundary table: B0 signing identity (reported), B1 permission grant (reported, at least privileged inferred), B2 caller validation in the service (hypothesis), B3 Bluetooth bond and link encryption (hypothesis), B4 vendor framing and session authentication (hypothesis). Each has an experiment.
Four-step isolating experiment: discovery, binding, authorization, execution, read off the first step that fails.
Target state machine: Disconnected, Discovering, Connecting, Connected, Initialising, Ready, with Failed from any state. Only Ready would accept commands. Not built.

records.title: stylo2/docs/I-evidence-ledger.md: claims and open questions
records.summary: Every route claim with a verified, reported or hypothesis label, plus eleven open questions that each name an exact experiment.
details: Path: stylo2/docs/I-evidence-ledger.md.
Its labels: [V] confirmed from the repository or a primary source (not the live device), [R] community or secondary, or this repository's reproduction of a vendor interface, [H] open.

Mapping used in this database: verified only where the code in this repository settles it; anything about device behaviour never run on a device is unverified; reported becomes unverified; hypothesis becomes inferred; open questions become open.
The ledger marks the owner's statement 'everything works except third-party haptics' as [V]. Here it is unverified: it is the owner's report and nothing has been run on a device.

records.title: stylo2/docs/MISSION.md: the interoperability brief
records.summary: The canonical brief for the non-root interoperability track: goal, non-negotiables, deliverable map, capture method and acceptance criteria.
details: Path: stylo2/docs/MISSION.md.

Goal: enable native Stylo 2 haptics in third-party apps on a stock, non-rooted OnePlus Pad 3 (OxygenOS 16, Android 16), or show with evidence which authorization boundary prevents it and what the least-restrictive legitimate alternative is.

Non-negotiables: no root, Magisk, KernelSU, bootloader unlock or system change; invent no keys, packet formats, UUIDs, permissions or authorization behaviour; keep feasibility, policy, risk and legal questions apart; do not misrepresent the app's identity.
Nine deliverables. The physical Pad 3 test report is pending hardware. The unresolved questions with an experiment each are in the evidence ledger (src-stylo2-i-evidence-ledger).
Method: nine controlled captures with a fixed recording schema, HCI snoop first, an external BLE sniffer only if the snoop is not enough.

Acceptance criteria: the cause is identified and evidenced, each verified profile selects, on and off are reliable, reconnection is handled, normal input and Notes keep working, no root or system change, nothing undocumented presented as fact.
State machine: the code ships five states (Disconnected, Connecting, Connected, PermissionDenied, ServiceUnavailable). The seven-state lifecycle is the target once a real session flow is verified.

It describes the test tablet as stock and non-rooted. The upstream README describes a tablet converted from OPD2413 to OPD2415, and PICKUP.md says the tablet's root and fix-module state is not established (dev-oneplus-pad3).

records.title: PICKUP.md: playbook for the local session with the Pad 3
records.summary: The ordered playbook for a Claude Code session with the Pad 3 attached: read-outs, the Route A run, the handshake, Route B, and where each result is recorded.
details: Path: PICKUP.md at the repository root. It replaces two earlier handoffs, the firmware read-out prompt and the route-testing brief.

Steps: 0 host baseline; 1 tablet check (read-only); 2 read-out and firmware retrieval (read-only); 3 Route A PoC (ask first, it installs an app); 4 attach handshake (guided); 5 Route B (ask first, turning on the HCI snoop log is a settings change and Shizuku and BlueShark are extra apps); 6 record and commit.

Tools it names: research/tools/pad3_readout.py (check, identify, firmware, modules, driver, service, bluetooth, handshake, poc-log, all) and research/tools/fwinfo.py. The read-out lands in research/local/pad3/, which git ignores.

Step 2 includes the protection level of safe.IOT, read two ways. Its expectation, not a result: if the level includes signature, an ordinary app can never hold the permission and Route A should fail at bind.

Its 'already known' list labels the path apps to com.oplus.ipemanager to Bluetooth LE to the pen as verified from the upstream app code and community sources. The code and README show the service talks to the pen over Bluetooth. Bluetooth LE and the channel come from the charger handshake log and are not shown by any code. This database keeps c-pen-attach-handshake inferred and gap-haptic-over-gatt open.
It says it is not established whether the tablet is rooted or has a pen-fix module. MISSION.md and stylo2/README.md describe the target as stock and non-rooted.

Rules in short: the tablet is read-only, root only for reads, ask before anything that changes the tablet, write to the pen only bytes captured from Notes, a route that needs a bypass is a finding, and works means the pen physically vibrated. The full rules are in CLAUDE.md (src-project-rules).
It has an unfilled marker for the ordered list of open questions. The route gaps in this database are written to fill it.
It says the Rust workspace has 26 passing tests, which matches the run on 2 Nov 2026.

records.title: XDA: OnePlus Stylo 2 global haptic feedback
records.summary: Discussion and install thread for the Stylo2 Haptics Magisk module and app, which is the project in this repository.
details: The repository README links this thread for discussion and install instructions.

Module: installs the app to /system/priv-app with a privapp-permissions allowlist on the system, system_ext and product partitions, so Android grants it com.oplus.permission.safe.IOT at boot. The README states that no firmware files are modified.
App: binds to com.oplus.ipemanager with the action com.oplus.ipemanager.ACTION.PENCIL_SDK and calls setVibrationType and startFeedBackVibration.

records.title: xiaomi-sheng-thp (Linux userspace pen and touch driver)
records.summary: Userspace driver for the Xiaomi Pad 6S Pro 12.4 ("sheng") on Linux. It shows pen position coming from the touch controller and pressure coming over Bluetooth.
details: Reads raw THP frames from the NT36532E touch controller through kernel nodes such as /proc/nvt_thp_stylus and exposes standard input devices through uinput.
Pen coordinates, tilt and hover come from the touch controller stream. Pen scanning works only at 60 Hz or 120 Hz panel refresh.
Pressure comes from the pen's Bluetooth HID reports (BlueZ required).
The Focus Pen Pro posture sensor is read separately through libssc.
No haptics support is mentioned.
C++20, Apache-2.0, runs as root, needs a kernel with the Xiaomi THP nodes.
records.basis: Project README read on 2 Nov 2026.
